projects.title: Ask GovAI — RAG over Federal AI Contracts
projects.description: A retrieval-augmented Q&A layer over a live index of 670+ U.S. federal AI/ML contract awards. BM25 lexical retrieval (key-free) feeds grounded, provider-agnostic LLM synthesis (free Gemini or Claude) with citations and a refuse-to-invent guardrail — backed by a measured eval harness (recall@8 = 92%; 69% BM25 baseline before the structured query router), not a demo.
highlights: Cost-aware by design: cheap lexical retrieval finds the documents; the LLM only synthesizes
Grounded answers cite the award_id and refuse when the dataset doesn't support a claim
Eval harness with a natural-language gold set — recall@8 = 92% measured (69% BM25 baseline; a structured query router fixed the superlative/NAICS misses); answer accuracy + cost scored with a key
Honest failure-mode analysis (superlative queries need a structured path) + a hybrid-retrieval roadmap
Zero dependencies — raw fetch, provider-agnostic synthesis (free Gemini or paid Claude)

projects.title: AI Interview & Fit-Scoring (Anna)
projects.description: An AI voice agent that interviews candidates in their language, then scores how well they fit a role from the transcript — across skills, experience, location, availability and tenure. I designed how it interviews and how the fit score is computed.
highlights: AI voice agent conducts a real, role-specific interview
Transcript scored into a fit score (interview weighted over the résumé)
Designed the interview structure and the scoring model
Live on a recruiting platform used by 10,000+ people

projects.title: MCP Directory — Zero-Touch Data Pipeline
projects.description: An automated index of ~1,800 metadata-verified Model Context Protocol servers. A weekly GitHub Actions cron searches, dedupes, filters, and classifies GitHub repos, commits the data, and redeploys the Astro static site — fully unattended since April 2026. An automation/ops project, deliberately not an AI one.
highlights: Weekly scrape -> filter -> classify -> commit -> deploy, zero-touch on GitHub Actions
Precision filter: a repo must identify itself as MCP in its own metadata (topic-spam from 100k-star unrelated repos gets rejected)
~1,800 static pages, client-side weighted search, programmatic SEO
Runs itself: the only human input since launch has been quality tuning

projects.title: Planning Desk: Agent Loop over MCP
projects.description: A chat interface that answers planning questions by calling real tools over MCP, with a second mode that turns two years of exchange-rate history into spreadsheets, documents and charts. The agent loop is one hand-written function, with no orchestration framework, over 3 MCP servers that run as child processes on stdio and expose 18 tools.
highlights: Hard ceilings on every turn: 8 steps, 12 tool calls, 60,000 tokens, and 45 seconds per tool call
A rules table decides feasibility, not the model, so the same question gets the same answer twice
Progress streams over SSE: each tool call shows in the page as it happens
Runs free on Render and Gemini's free tier, with a Cloudflare Worker in front of Open-Meteo, which refused calls from Render's shared outbound address
187 tests that need no network, API key or model

projects.title: IndiaTenders: Open Government Tenders, Searchable
projects.description: A free, searchable index of open Indian government tenders from the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP), deduplicated, categorised and sorted by closing date. Tender-intelligence subscriptions charge thousands of rupees a year for this data, which is public.
highlights: A cron scrapes a bounded number of the newest CPPP list pages every 6 hours, about 1.5 seconds apart, and builds coverage across runs
The parser is pure and unit-tested against a saved copy of the real page
Data-quality gates: a run that parses nothing fails instead of publishing, and one that would shrink the dataset below 70% refuses to overwrite
Tests and the build run before each data commit, so bad data blocks the publish
A static page per tender and organisation, plus CSV and JSON exports, RSS and a sitemap
